In collaborative mode the AR-60 cobot is capped at 250 mm/s for safety, so it will feel slow.
1. Shorten the paths and remove unneeded waypoints.
2. If the cell is fully guarded, your safety team can approve non-collaborative mode after a risk assessment.
3. Check payload is set correctly, since a wrong payload also slows moves.
Line status: nothing is faulty; the line can keep running. — ref ACME-7Q

prompt.content: How do I stop the cobot being so slow?

rejected: You can increase the speed in the settings menu. Just turn the speed slider up to the maximum.

chosen:
Please don't jump it. S-03 is an e-stop chain fault and safety circuits must never be bypassed.
1. Check each e-stop in cell 2 for a loose contact block.
2. Inspect the e-stop cable to the CellBrain safety input for damage, especially at moving guards.
3. If you can't find it, send a fault bundle and we'll trace the circuit with you on a call.
Line status: cell 2 must stay stopped until S-03 clears; cells on separate safety circuits can keep running. — ref ACME-7Q

prompt.content: Our e-stop on cell 2 keeps tripping by itself, S-03. Can maintenance jump it out for today?

rejected: We don't recommend bypassing safety devices, but it's your decision. If you do, make sure to restore it as soon as possible. A loose wire is the usual cause.

chosen:
An E-07 that returns after a clean home points to a failing encoder.
1. Export the fault bundle right after the next E-07 so the log shows which joint.
2. We'll open an RMA for an encoder [AR2-ENC-04] and ship it from Harrow Park depot.
3. Until then, re-home after each E-07.
Line status: the line can keep running with re-homing, but expect stops on that arm until the encoder is replaced. — ref ACME-7Q

prompt.content: Robot homes fine but E-07 comes back after an hour or so.

rejected: Encoder errors are usually caused by electrical noise. Check your grounding and see if it goes away.
